cells.tense: You are holding the pen right now and aiming it where you mean to.
cells.ask: Before you explain one thing today, strip it to the single fact that would still be true if nobody agreed with you.
cells.core:
You can see the shape of a problem before anyone else has finished describing it. That's not a party trick. It means when you aim your attention, it lands — this, not that, and the thinking follows.

What keeps this real is that it rests on something built, not borrowed. The work is done; the thinking has somewhere to stand. So the aim doesn't need defending before it goes out. You can let a good thing you've worked out show, without first checking whether it's allowed to be good. Point the reasoning at something that matters to you, not just at whatever's in front of you. Let one piece of finished thinking leave the notebook and go somewhere it can be used — and let that be enough for now.

cells.tense: You are bracing for a future where the logic must already have won.
cells.ask: Pick the one decision you keep re-arguing. Write it, date it, and for one day treat it as settled — no revisiting, no refinements.
cells.core:
You're running the argument ahead of the room. A conversation gets treated as a problem to be solved before it's started, and the solving has gotten louder than whatever it was for. The thinking is good. It's just working on a future that isn't here, and it can't win a race with something that hasn't happened.

You don't need more reasoning. You need a decision that holds its shape. One call, stated plainly, stood behind without another pass through the logic. Limits around what's yours to think about and what isn't — set once and left alone. The clear structure is the point. When things have a boundary you're not constantly redrawing, the reasoning gets somewhere to rest instead of somewhere to run.

cells.tense: You were at the door when it mattered and you are still standing there.
cells.ask: Say one thing out loud to someone who wasn't in the room when you figured it out — tell it straight, no preamble and no memo.
cells.core:
The sharpness is still there. You just stopped turning it toward anything, and from the outside it can look like there's nothing to turn it toward. So the reasoning goes quiet, or it circles, or it waits for a better moment that doesn't arrive.

The ability is still in you. What's gone quiet is the charge — something to move toward through the thinking. So don't push the thinking itself. Find one piece of meaning other people share and carry it to them: say it, teach it, make a small ritual out of it. Not a lecture. Something you actually mean, passed to one person. When the meaning moves, the aim comes back. The reasoning only needs something to move toward.

cells.tense: The pen is already down and the writing is happening in a room you are not standing in.
cells.ask: Take one call you've been calling the situation's, the team's, or just how it is — and say out loud, to yourself, 'I decided that.'
cells.core:
The steering is happening. The reasoning is doing the work — sorting, cutting, pointing where things go — and it gets described as just how the situation is. It runs either way. What's missing is your name on it.

That's not a character flaw. It's a habit of claiming: the thinking got so natural that it stopped feeling like a choice. So go back to the simpler thing. Notice one decision you made that shaped something, and hold it as yours without either inflating it or handing it off to the room. You don't have to claim everything. One clean admission that you steered will do more than a whole analysis of why you might have. The credit is already earned. The saying so is the only part left.
cells.sheetLine: The steering is happening. You just haven't signed it.
